newsitem.title: USA: Roland says multimedia chipmakers held in contempt.
newsitem.headline: Roland says multimedia chipmakers held in contempt.

text.p: Roland Corp said a U.S. District court ruled several leading suppliers of multimedia chips had violated a preliminary injunction barring new sales of goods containing Roland sound recordings and trademarks.
Among those named in the suit were semiconductor makers Atmel Corp and its French-based Dream SA unit, and Crystal Semiconductor Co, a unit of Cirrus Logic Inc.

Roland, a well-known maker of electronic music products, said the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California on March 10, 1997 issued a finding of civil contempt of court against the chipmakers.
The company said U.S. District Court Judge Dickran Tevrizian ruled that Atmel, Dream and Crystal had violated a preliminary injunction entered December 30, 1996.

Roland said the defendants had appealed the preliminary injunction to the U.S. Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals but that both courts had denied motions by the defendants to stay the preliminary injunction pending the appeal.
Atmel and Cirrus Logic could not immediately be reached for comment.

Roland said it had registered a copyright in a series of sound recordings of musical instruments and sound effects fixed in a digital memory chip. Appplications for the copyrighted sound recordings include electronic musical instruments, computer sound cards and karaoke machines.
